title: Processing of identified data

title: Identifier in data

title: Revealing attributes

title: Unique identifier linking

title: Quasi-identifier combining

title: Data type sensitivity

title: Linking through unique identifier in parent account data
description: Parent account information may contain unique identifiers that can be used to link this data to other records or data subjects, potentially enabling cross-referencing with other systems or databases.

title: Processing of identified data for parent account storage
description: The authentication service processes and stores parent account information which contains identified data that can be used to identify specific individuals.

title: Identifier in parent account data
description: Parent account information may contain unique identifiers (such as account IDs, usernames, or other unique references) that can be used to identify the data subject.

title: Data can be used to prevent denial of claims
description: Stored parent account data can be used to prevent an individual from denying certain claims about their account or actions, as the data provides evidence of their identity and actions.

title: Existence of parent account revealed in system response
description: The existence of a parent account record may be revealed in system responses (e.g., error messages, access logs) which can be used to detect the presence of specific data subjects.

title: Data type sensitivity - parent account data may be more sensitive than required
description: Parent account information may contain more sensitive data types than functionally required by the authentication system, potentially including personal identifiers beyond what is needed for authentication.

title: Treatment of parent account data may not be necessary
description: The treatment, analysis, or enrichment of parent account data may not be necessary to achieve the functional goals of the authentication system.

title: Data subject unawareness of parent account storage
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their parent account information is being collected, stored, and processed by the authentication service.

title: Lack of control over parent account data processing
description: Data subjects may lack control over how their parent account information is processed, stored, and retained by the authentication service.

title: Insufficient data subject controls for parent account data
description: Support for data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure) regarding parent account information may be lacking, potentially violating GDPR requirements.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data may be processed for parent account storage than is actually needed for the authentication functionality.

title: Linking through JWT identifier
description: JWT token contains unique identifier that can be used to link data across systems and identify the user
assumptions: JWT typically contains user ID or token that is unique to the user

title: Processing of user identifier in JWT
description: Authentication service processes and transmits unique identifier through JWT token to child user
assumptions: JWT contains unique user reference that can identify the data subject

title: Unnecessary sensitive data in JWT
description: JWT may contain more sensitive data than functionally required for authentication purposes
assumptions: JWT may include user profile data beyond authentication needs
uncertainty_note: JWT scope may vary - some implementations include minimal claims, others include full profile data

title: Excessive video metadata collection
description: Video metadata may include more sensitive data types than functionally required for video management service operations.
assumptions: Assumes video metadata collection includes user identifiers, timestamps, and other potentially sensitive information beyond basic video file management.

title: Excessive volume of video data processed
description: The MongoDB videos collection may process a large volume of video metadata and files beyond what is functionally needed for the video management service.
assumptions: Assumes the system stores all video metadata and files rather than only necessary information.

title: Data propagation to external services
description: Video metadata and files may be propagated to other services where they are not needed, increasing exposure risk.
assumptions: Assumes the video management service may share or propagate data to other systems.

title: Unique identifiers in video metadata
description: Video metadata may contain unique references to the identity of data subjects (e.g., user IDs, account identifiers) that could be used to identify individuals.
assumptions: Assumes video metadata includes user-specific identifiers.

title: Revealing attributes in video data
description: Video files and metadata may contain revealing attributes that support identification of data subjects (e.g., timestamps, location data, user behavior patterns).
assumptions: Assumes video data may contain attributes that can be used to identify individuals.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data is processed than is actually needed for the video management service functionality.
assumptions: Assumes the system collects and stores more data than functionally required.

title: Unawareness of video data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their video metadata and files are being collected, stored, and processed by the video management service.
assumptions: Assumes users may not be informed about the extent of data collection for video management.

title: Profiling of child through search and watch history
description: Search and watch history data can be analyzed to create profiles of children's interests, behaviors, and patterns, which can be linked to the child's identity and potentially used for targeted advertising or other profiling purposes.

title: Search history contains unique identifiers
description: Child search and watch history is processed and stored, potentially containing unique identifiers that can identify the specific child as a data subject.

title: Revealing attributes in search history
description: Search and watch history contains revealing attributes about the child's interests, age group, and preferences that can support identification of the data subject.

title: Attributable data evidence from search history
description: Search and watch history records can be used to attribute specific actions and behaviors to a particular child, preventing the child from denying certain claims about their activities.

title: Detection through observed communications
description: Search and watch history can be detected through system responses and observed communications, potentially revealing the existence of the child's data.

title: Sensitive data type collected
description: Search and watch history is considered sensitive personal data that should only be collected and processed when strictly required for the functional purpose of child profile management.

title: Excessive volume of search history
description: The volume of search and watch history processed may exceed what is functionally needed for the child profile management system.

title: Unnecessary treatment of search history
description: Search and watch history may be further treated, analyzed, or enriched in ways that are not necessary to achieve the functionality of the child profile management system.

title: Data accessible to more parties than necessary
description: Child search and watch history may be made accessible to more parties than functionally necessary for the child profile management system.

title: Unawareness of processing by children
description: Children may not be aware that their search and watch history is being collected, processed, stored, or disclosed.

title: Lack of control over data processing preferences
description: Parents or guardians may lack control over how their child's search and watch history is processed, stored, or disclosed.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (search and watch history) is processed than is actually needed for the functional purpose of child profile management.

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: Support for data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure) may be lacking for child search and watch history data.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The authentication service processes government ID images which contain identifiable information about individuals.
assumptions: Government ID images contain personal identifiers that can be used to identify individuals.

title: Processing of identifiable information
description: The system processes identifiable information from which the identity of the data subject may be derived through government ID images.
assumptions: Government ID images can be used to identify or link to specific individuals.

title: Data can be used to prevent denial of claims
description: Stored government ID images can be used to attribute actions or claims to specific individuals, preventing them from denying certain activities.
assumptions: The stored images can be retrieved and used as evidence of identity.

title: Existence of data reveals system involvement
description: The existence of government ID image files in the system reveals that specific individuals are using the authentication service.
assumptions: File system access patterns or file existence can be observed.

title: Data type sensitivity
description: Government ID images are highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected and processed when strictly required for the authentication service.
assumptions: The authentication service may not strictly require storing full government ID images.

title: Data propagation to other services
description: Stored government ID images may be accessible or propagated to other services where they are not functionally needed.
assumptions: The file system backend/uploads/ may be accessible to other services.

title: Unawareness of processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their government ID images are being stored and processed by the authentication service.
assumptions: Users may not be informed about the storage of their ID images.

title: Lack of control over data erasure
description: Data subjects may lack control to request removal or rectification of their stored government ID images.
assumptions: The system may not support data subject rights for erasure of stored images.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Government ID images may be processed in excess of what is actually needed for the authentication service functionality.
assumptions: The authentication service may not require full government ID image storage.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Government ID images may be stored longer than functionally needed for the authentication service.
assumptions: The system may not have defined retention policies for ID images.

title: Linking through JWT identifier
description: JWT tokens contain unique identifiers that can be used to link user sessions and activities across different interactions with the authentication service.
assumptions: JWTs typically contain user IDs or session identifiers that are unique to the data subject.

title: JWT contains unique identifier
description: The JWT token contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject, which is processed and stored in the browser.
assumptions: JWTs are designed to contain claims about the subject including unique identifiers.

title: JWT provides evidence of authentication
description: The JWT can be used to prevent an individual from denying that they performed certain actions or authenticated with the system.
assumptions: JWTs are cryptographically signed and can be verified to prove the identity of the holder.

title: JWT presence reveals authentication
description: The existence of a JWT in localStorage reveals that the user has authenticated with the system, which can be detected by observing the data store.
assumptions: JWTs are stored in localStorage as part of the authentication flow.

title: JWT accessible to multiple parties
description: localStorage is accessible to all scripts running in the browser context, meaning the JWT may be accessed by more parties than functionally necessary.
assumptions: localStorage is a browser API that allows any script to read/write data.

title: JWT publicly accessible in localStorage
description: Data stored in localStorage is publicly accessible within the browser context and can be read by any script, including malicious ones.
assumptions: localStorage does not provide access controls beyond the same-origin policy.

title: User unaware of JWT storage
description: Users may not be aware that their JWT is being stored in localStorage, which is not a typical or expected storage location for authentication tokens.
assumptions: Users typically expect tokens to be stored in memory or cookies, not localStorage.

title: User cannot easily remove JWT
description: Users may not know how to remove JWTs from localStorage, making it difficult to exercise their right to erasure or rectification.
assumptions: localStorage management is not exposed to users through standard browser interfaces.

title: Violation of data minimization
description: Storing JWTs in localStorage may process more personal data than functionally needed, as the token contains identifying information that could be minimized.
assumptions: JWTs contain more data than strictly necessary for authentication purposes.
